x: Pam and John married in 1960 and for these two setting up home together was not going to cramp their athletic style. Although he was not racing so much John was often encouraged by Pam to get out for a run.

John Stow and Pam were married in September with many Belgravians present. It seems confusion was caused by Gordon Biscoe handing out numbers and pins at the reception while Colin Pearson spent half the time looking for the changing rooms!
John too had family support for Pam and the boys were at the track to welcome him in. It was good to see another Davies family supporting the lads, Stan (up to town from Suffolk) and Dai.

Finishing as she did only a little before 1.50pm, Pam realised that there was no time to change. So she carried on running through the finishing line and into the football club Members Bar, still in vest and shorts.

We must mention one of his other highlights, which was of course meeting Pam while training at Tooting. Pam, an International herself, must surely share in the credit for the honour of Life Membership bestowed upon John — for keeping our boy on the straight and narrow all this time!

I remember the times when, at Baron's Court at the Couzens' family home, Bill, George Stanley, Pam's 'husband to be' and myself would drive his parents and sisters Pam and Sylvia crazy with our attempts to play skiffle, imitating Lonnie Donegan.
